items.note: A lemon hero band in the content column: a 96px two-line headline, a centred lead, a black CTA paired with an outline button at the same height, and four different thick ink-outlined stickers (wallet, pencil, stopwatch, key). Below it come four band-colour vignette cards, a framed code block, a pink closing band and a black footer. This is clearly 01's language and page stack, but the stickers are about 130–150px against 01's 200–260px coins, and the bottom pair sit small in the corners, so the ring weighs less against the headline than in the reference.

The phone keeps the lemon hero, the hero headline, stacked black and outline actions and four stickers cropped by the side edges, then single-column vignette cards, a pink closing band and a black footer. It is close to 09/10's stacked bands, but the lead and both actions run flush to the screen edges with no side gutter.

This is a faithful 11-style inversion: black chrome, a black sidebar with a white current pill, a lemon band and stickers unchanged, the CTA turned pink, cards with a raised dark body under unchanged colour vignettes, and the pink closing band kept. The header's trailing action is a dark-grey hairline cell rather than 11's solid pink full-height block.

The phone hero in dark keeps the lemon band, the stickers, the pink CTA and the white outline button on the band, all over black chrome, as 11 does. The edge-to-edge actions and the two-row header carry over from the light phone.

A compact lemon header band holds the breadcrumb, a section-size title and the lead, with even padding over a paper body. The black current pill sits in the sidebar, package-manager tabs are outline pills, code blocks are ink-framed with a ruled caption bar and a Copy button, and the callouts are white ink panels (the warning has a 2px danger border). It reads like 06/07's product chrome, and the band no longer stretches to fit a sticker.

The band, breadcrumb and title stack cleanly on paper, like 10's lemon header band. The top bar is crude next to 10's single-row band: it breaks into two rows, the search shrinks beside a half-height bordered cell for one link, and the second link floats loose beneath it.

The same compact lemon band sits over black, with a white current pill, raised dark code boxes with 35% white hairlines, and outline pills for package managers. Chrome inverts and bands stay, as 11 does.
The lemon band keeps its ink text on black, followed by the page-contents list and prose in light text. The inversion is right; the layout and the two-row header are the same as the light phone.

This area takes the periwinkle band (lemon, then periwinkle, in nav order), so colour means place as the spec intends. Under it sit ink-framed tables with bold heads and ruled rows, framed code and callouts. The option tables are crudely proportioned: Type and Default columns get wide air while the description is squeezed into 3–4-line wraps, where 07/08 keep rows even and calm.
A periwinkle band and a ruled page-contents list lead to framed code and tables. The option tables are cramped to phone width: rows grow very tall and the description column is cut off at the frame.
The periwinkle band is unchanged over black, with a white current pill, raised dark code and table boxes and white hairlines. It is a correct 11-style inversion of the light page.

The periwinkle band sits over black, followed by an open page-contents list of ten underlined links that fills the rest of the first screen before any content. 10 puts the screen's controls in one compact row instead.

A lemon header band with one thick tag sticker cropped by the trailing edge. Each release is a white ink box divided by ruled rows, with outline status pills holding a coloured dot and a pink notched 'new' flag on the latest. This is strong use of the flag and pill vocabulary, but the band runs about 120px of empty lemon below the lead to fit the sticker, where 06's band closes soon after its content.

The band holds the title, the lead and the tag sticker cropped by the right edge. The release box keeps its ruled rows, status pills and the pink flag at phone width, close to 10's header band and stacked boxes.

Black chrome with the white current nav pill in the top bar; the lemon band, sticker and pink flag are unchanged; release boxes are raised dark with 35% white rules. It matches 11's rule that only the chrome inverts.

The lemon band, the sticker and the pink flag hold on black, and release boxes are raised dark with visible rules and dot pills. It is faithful to 11; the header shows the same two-row break as the other phone screens.

findings.summary: The hero's sticker ring is light. The four stickers are about 130–150px, against 01's 200–260px coins, the two lower ones are small in the corners, and one is cut by the bottom seam to about half. Next to a 96px headline the ring does not weigh against it as 01's coins do.
On the phone, the hero lead and both stacked actions run flush to the screen edges with no side gutter.

On phones the top bar breaks into two rows: the search shrinks beside a half-height bordered cell for one link, and the second link floats below it. The menu button exists, but the links were not moved into it.
On the phone, option tables cut the description column at the frame and grow very tall rows. There is no sticky first column, no scroll cue and no ruled-list fallback.

The overview's header band is about 250px tall for a title and a one-line lead, leaving about 120px of empty lemon under the lead. It is sized by the spec's sticker rule (min-height = sticker + padding), not by its content. 06's band closes right after its controls. Content-led bands, as on the installation and configuration pages, already read better.
findings.promptFix: Size a header band from its content plus space.6–space.8 padding, never from its sticker. Fit the sticker to the band's content height, and let the seam crop it rather than growing the band.
findings.specRule: .ft-band--with-sticker { --ft-s: clamp(var(--size-sticker-sm), 14vw, var(--size-sticker-band)); overflow: hidden; min-height: calc(var(--ft-s) + var(--space-6) * 2);

findings.summary: The header's trailing action is a plain hairline cell: white in light and dark grey in dark. 01 makes it a solid black full-height block and 11 a solid pink one, which anchors the header's right end.

Option tables split their width badly. The type and default columns get wide air while the description column wraps to 3–4 lines, so rows are uneven and tall. The reference's dense screens (07, 08) keep rows even and calm inside the ink frame.

On phones the page-contents list is fully open above the content: a ruled column of up to ten underlined links that fills the first screen. The spec's layout rules ask for a pill row or a top disclosure, and 10 keeps its controls in one compact row so the content shows first.
